scope: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B as a drop-in backbone for the text harness: chunked prefill, model-generic generation, first frozen-suite result.

prefill.graph: qwen36_prefill.jl: one semantic graph per chunk width; projections, router, experts, shared experts and combine over the chunk's columns; recurrent and attention state column by column with the decode kernels
new_kernels: Q5_K product over columns (routed kernel, one expert per column)
prefill.shared_with_decode: declare_experts! (gate/up, SwiGLU or SwiGLU+Q8, down) is the decode graph's

chunk32_default_35b_radeon.note: 20 columns take the fp16 K-quant GEMM

throughput_tok_s_radeon_256_tokens.protocol: median of 3 interleaved rounds after a warm-up round, default optimizations, idle GPU

harness.text_backbone.jl: textsession/ingest!/feed!/generate!/describe per model type; loadbackbone and loadtokenizer take a model directory or a GGUF
harness.tokenizer: Qwen3.5 tokenizer.json is an exact prefix of the GGUF vocabulary; the 250 extra ids are 7 audio/TTS control tokens and 243 padding entries; merges and EOS/BOS identical; plain-text chat template subset identical
harness.regression_found: the harness ingested prompts with chunk=32; since >16-column products take the fp16 K-quant GEMM this no longer reproduced frozen Qwen3.5 receipts (stable_groups 150 -> 136 tokens)
harness.fix: ingest! uses the GEMV width for both families
harness.head_layout_bug: Qwen3.6 sessions defaulted to the native recurrent head order; GGUF weights need tiled and decoded garbage without it. The default now comes from the checkpoint.

julia_tasks_frozen_protocol.settings: greedy, 512-token budget, no thinking, same prompts and private contracts
julia_tasks_frozen_protocol.conclusion: the suite is saturated by Qwen3.6; it cannot measure repair or evidence interventions on this backbone

fixes_outside_the_runner.tools/measure.jl: telemetry resolved at the first reading (Base.OncePerProcess), and a machine without /sys/class/drm reaches the documented refusal; SmallLLMChecks failed to load on macOS with an IOError before. Test: tools/test_measure.jl
fixes_outside_the_runner.BonsaiRunner depthwise_conv4_batch_kerne: SiLU written as the decode kernel's y*(1/(1+exp(-y))); y/(1+exp(-y)) rounded an ulp apart on Metal, so chunked prefill drifted from sequential decode there. Test: bitwise chunking check in test_state_boundaries.jl
fixes_outside_the_runner.Mantle access walk: dynamic-call refusals name the callee (getglobal/GlobalRef resolved) and report a missing module member; test in Mantle/test/test_access.jl; Radeon access tests 70/70. Not synced to the Mac, whose Mantle checkout has its own uncommitted work

kernel_study_transfers.driver: transfer_studies.jl + transfer_kernel_studies.jl: new registrations that reuse the original packets' tasks, prompts, private contracts and sampler (checked by hash) and record overrides, sources and backbone; original packets untouched

frozen_budget_2048_thinking.qwen36: 0/4, all four truncated while thinking, with essentially correct kernels in the reasoning

budget_6144_feedback.fixed_by_feedback: column_major_scale (kernel did not end in return nothing)
still_failing: affine: `using KernelInterface as KI` is invalid syntax; the feedback arm thought past 6144 tokens
atomic_max: calls Atomix.atomic_max, which does not exist; the API is the macro Atomix.@atomic

named_callee_rerun.change: Mantle access-walk refusals name the callee and say when a module does not define it (was: 'a call to `%12`')
named_callee_rerun.result: still failed: the model switched to Atomix.atomic_max!, another nonexistent name; an API it does not know is not supplied by a better error message

kernel_study_transfers.caveat: four authored development tasks, one sampled attempt each; direction, not significance
